answers: A New Orleans judge officially approved Robert Durst's February plea deal on a gun charge and sentenced him to seven years in prison on Wednesday, Reuters reports. For more than a year, the real estate heir has languished in a New Orleans prison after being nabbed with a handgun in his hotel room. He was busted for that felony just one day before the series finale of HBO's The Jinx, in which he famously appeared to confess to three murders by saying, "What the hell did I do? Killed them all, of course." US District Judge Kurt Engelhardt also agreed that Durst can be transferred to a low-security prison with medical facilities in San Pedro, Calif., where the 73-year-old's attorneys say his "advanced age and poor health" can be better addressed, per the Advocate. In California, Durst will face a murder charge in the 2000 death of friend Susan Berman, the AP reports. (A Texas judge believes Durst once dumped a cat's head on her doorstep.)

**Summary of News on Robert Durst**

Robert Durst, a wealthy New York real estate heir and long-time suspect in multiple murders, was sentenced to seven years in federal prison on a gun charge in New Orleans on April 27, 2016. The sentence, which includes 85 months in prison followed by three years of supervised release, was part of a plea agreement that also resolved pending charges in New York, Texas, and Louisiana. Durst, 73, pleaded guilty in February to being a felon in possession of a firearm after a search of his hotel room in New Orleans uncovered a loaded revolver, marijuana, and other items. He has been held in Louisiana since his arrest in March 2015.

Durst is expected to be transferred to California within weeks to face a murder charge in the 2000 death of his friend Susan Berman. He has consistently denied killing her, claiming he is innocent and that he wants to defend himself in the case. His attorneys have requested that he be housed at a low-security federal prison in Los Angeles, near the location of his upcoming trial. The judge, Kurt Engelhardt, has agreed to recommend this transfer, which would allow Durst to be arraigned in Los Angeles on August 18.

Durst’s case has been the subject of intense public and media scrutiny, particularly following the release of the HBO documentary series *The Jinx*, which chronicled his alleged involvement in the 2003 murder of his neighbor Morris Black and the 1982 disappearance of his wife, Kathleen. In the final episode of the series, Durst was recorded muttering, “I killed them all,” which has fueled speculation about his guilt. However, his attorneys have maintained that he is not responsible for Berman’s death and that the case remains unsolved.

Durst has a history of legal troubles, including previous convictions for jumping bail and carrying a weapon across state lines in 2004. He served three years in prison for those charges. Prosecutors allege that Durst, who is worth an estimated $100 million, killed Berman to prevent her from talking to authorities about the disappearance of his wife. Despite these claims, Durst’s defense team remains confident in his innocence and believes he will be exonerated in the upcoming trial.
